Which Type of Wire Should I Use for My EDM?
Mitsubishi wire edm MV maintenance part 1
NEXT Generation Mitsubishi MV Series Wire EDM

features: Fiber optic drive communication (4x faster than previous generation)
Dry automatic wire threading (14-inch annealed wire, threads through slots/counterbores)
Power Master (adaptive power for variable flush conditions)
MV1200S.targetMarket: Small job shops, mold makers, toolrooms
MV1200S.notes: Best-selling Mitsubishi wire EDM in UK market. Same control/casting platform as R-series.

driveSystem.type: Full linear motor on all 4 axes

features: Tubular drive on U and V axes (vs ball screw on S model)

lowerRollerBearings.procedure: Full disassembly, ultrasonic clean, rebuild with new bearings. Left-hand threads on roller unit to prevent wire-induced loosening.

diamondGuides.procedure: Use guide wrench (U for upper, D for lower). Clean with ultrasonic. Be careful with ceramic isolator — shatters if dropped.

powerFeeders.notes: Check for groove wear. Upper and lower power feeders transfer electrical current to wire.

fullTeardown.procedure: Complete upper and lower head disassembly. Run all internals through ultrasonic tank. Replace worn bearings, seals, springs. Check roller play — wobble or thrust indicates bad bearings.

threadingDiagnostics.symptoms: Wire jumps at lower roller, machine stops during threading
threadingDiagnostics.rootCause: Lower roller bearing wear — shaft play/wobble
threadingDiagnostics.fix: Replace lower roller bearings and wave spring washer

MV2400S.notes: Same platform as MV1200S with larger work envelope

features: Full tubular drive on all axes
MV2400R.notes: Used in wire type comparison test (video 2vP73mA2yQo)

controlSystem.name: Advanced Plus 3 Control (M800 series)
controlSystem.manufacturer: Mitsubishi Electric (2nd largest control producer worldwide)

workpiecePickup: Work slope detection (auto-alignment to machine axes, eliminates manual clocking)
programInput: DXF file import (via network or USB)

steps: 1. Import geometry (DXF/IGES via USB or network)
2. Sample outline from solid model (outside contour extraction)
3. Transfer to 2D CAM system on control
5. Move to CAM — specify thread location and workpiece height
6. Set conditions: answer guided prompts for material, thickness, wire type, desired surface finish
7. Technology search: control finds optimal generator settings, offsets, stepping increments
8. Configure strategy: die/punch shape, single/multiple parts, cutting strategy
9. Apply process and generate NC program
10. Optional: open editor for program modifications
11. Move to Monitor screen and start cutting

cornerControl.roughCut: Automatic corner management — adjusts power at sharp corners to prevent wire lag
cornerControl.skimCut: Wire can be forced deeper into corners for improved accuracy
cornerControl.punchMode: Takes more of the radius for punch tooling applications, reduces bench work

technologyFeatures.masterShapeControl: Handles differences between straight and curved surfaces automatically

powerMaster.purpose: Adaptive power control for variable flushing conditions
powerMaster.use: Enable when: poor flushing, changing Z depths, variable workpiece thickness
powerMaster.disable: For best speed comparison testing with good flush conditions

eAdjust.notes: Can be moved up 3 notches with premium wire to increase cutting speed

maintenanceFeatures.maintenanceTimers: On-screen alerts for lubrication oil, filter changes, and wire remaining
maintenanceFeatures.wireRemaining: Estimates wire left on spool for overnight/unattended runs
maintenanceFeatures.threadingManagement: Real-time wire thread tracking with PDF troubleshooting guides built into control
maintenanceFeatures.guideDiagnostics: PDF-based visual guide system for fault resolution

dCubesSoftware.name: D-CUBES
dCubesSoftware.status: Video ROVXHOG3SHs unavailable — limited data from other sources
knownFeatures: DXF/IGES geometry import and outline sampling
Automatic technology selection based on material/thickness/wire
NC program generation with multi-pass strategy
Simple Figures feature for basic shape programming

characteristics: Adequate surface finish for most applications

testResult_quarterInch_hole_1875thick.notes: Rough + finish + 3 skim passes, good flush condition, MV2400R

characteristics: Zinc coating provides better spark characteristics
Faster cutting speed than straight brass
Better surface finish than straight brass

premiumZincCoated.composition: Brass core with premium/stratified zinc coating
characteristics: Highest cost option (56% more than brass)
Allows lower wire feed rate (from 8 to 6 on MV control)
Up to 30% wire consumption reduction on rough cut
E-condition can be increased 3 notches for more speed

testResult_quarterInch_hole_1875thick.notes: Same standard settings as other wires. Additional speed possible with wire-specific E-adjust optimization.

factorsToConsider: Wire cost vs machine time cost (hourly rate)
Number of machines (single machine = maximize throughput)
Production volume (high volume with good flush = premium wire payback is faster)
Flushing conditions (good flush = premium wire benefits shine)
Part complexity and number of start holes
selectionGuidance.keyInsight: Wire is the biggest running cost on a wire EDM. The wire cost difference ($165 vs $258 per spool) is often offset by faster cutting and reduced wire consumption, especially with consistent good flushing.
selectionGuidance.testConclusion: On a 3/8" diameter hole through 1.875" D2 tool steel: Premium zinc coated = 42:33, Zinc coated = 43:22, Straight brass = 46:54. All produced acceptable fit on ejector pins.

wireSpeed.notes: Digital anti-electrolysis enables lower wire speed without quality loss

wireConsumption.notes: V350 generator pulse shaping + fiber optic servo response reduces electrode wear dramatically

roughCut.cornerManagement: Automatic power reduction at sharp corners to prevent wire lag and breakage

skimPasses.typicalCount: 3 skim passes after rough cut for precision work
skimPasses.strategy: Rough cut + finish + 3 skims for ejector pin holes
skimPasses.offsetStepping: Control automatically calculates offset reductions per skim pass

flushingPressure.goodCondition: Both upper and lower flush cups sealed against workpiece, submerged cutting
flushingPressure.poorCondition: Open top, slots, variable thickness — use Power Master
flushingPressure.impact: Good flushing = faster cutting, fewer wire breaks, better surface finish
flushingPressure.notes: When comparing wires, turn Power Master OFF for apples-to-apples comparison under good flush

materialThickness.interpolation: For workpiece between standard thicknesses, select next larger setting
materialThickness.tallParts: Mitsubishi technology excels with tall workpieces, multiple holes, step changes
materialThickness.typicalRange_mm: 20-30mm is 'quite a nice situation' for standard cutting

tubularDrive.principle: Permanent magnets arranged as buttons inside stainless steel tube, 360-degree magnetic flux
advantages: No contact — zero wear, zero backlash
No cogging (smooth motion at all speeds)
No heat transfer to machine casting
Immune to metallic shop dust interference
Higher speed and precision than ball screws
12-year positional warranty (vs 10-year for ball screw models)
tubularDrive.comparison: Replaces both ball screws AND flat-plate linear motors. Flat plate systems had: large magnets, special casting requirements, heat trapped behind iron backplate, susceptible to dust.

servoControl.purpose: EDM process happens in microseconds — fiber optics enable real-time gap feedback and adjustment
servoControl.notes: Information transmitted from drive system to servo and back at optical speed

features: Digital Matrix Sensor for gap monitoring
generator.wireConsumptionReduction: Up to 60% reduction vs previous generation

digitalAntiElectrolysis.principle: Moves spark position in real time to distribute erosion evenly around wire circumference
benefits: Eliminates uneven power contactor wear (normally one wears faster than the other)
Enables 30% wire speed reduction without loss of cutting speed
Reduces overall wire consumption — biggest running cost on wire EDM
digitalAntiElectrolysis.impact_on_cost: Wire is the biggest running cost. 30% reduction = significant annual savings.

autoThreading.method: Kink-anneal: wire is kinked and annealed straight for insertion
capabilities: Thread through slots (not possible with wet/water jet threading)
Re-thread after wire break in closed path
autoThreading.comparisonToWetThreading: Wet threading (water jet) deflects the wire — cannot thread through slots, tapered surfaces, or counterbores. Dry threading overcomes all these limitations.

features: X and Y axes mounted directly on separate sets of ways on base casting
Table moves left-right on one set of ways (X)
Column moves in-out on separate center ways (Y)
Direct axis mounting eliminates squareness and repeatability issues from stacked table designs

table.notes: MV1200 machines are twice as heavy as previous generation models

machineConstruction.travelIncrease: Larger travel size without significant increase in machine footprint

daily: Check deionized water level and conductivity
weekly_80_100_hours: Clean power feeders (upper and lower) — check for groove wear
Check and clean flush cups and O-rings
monthly_200_250_hours: Full upper and lower head teardown
Run all internal components through ultrasonic cleaner
Inspect and replace lower roller bearings if needed
Clean ceramic isolator plates (handle carefully — shatters if dropped)
Inspect and clean wire path (rollers, guides, nozzles)
as_needed_500_hours: Replace power feeders when grooves appear
Replace diamond guides when wear is visible
criticalTips: Keep spare lower roller bearing kits on hand — when they fail, the machine stops
Use the wrenches that came with the machine for guide removal — prevents over-torque
Left-hand threads on lower roller assembly — turn clockwise to remove
Apply thin film of lubricant to shaft seal area during reassembly to prevent tearing
Check control maintenance timer screens regularly for upcoming service alerts
Ultrasonic cleaning is recommended for all disassembled parts

moldMaking.typicalWorkflow: Fast hole (start hole) machine → Wire EDM → Bench work
moldMaking.surfaceRequirements: Ra 0.3-0.4 um on steel, Ra 0.3 um on carbide

toolAndDie.punchVsDie: Control has punch mode that takes more radius to reduce bench work
toolAndDie.cornerControl: Skim cuts can force wire deeper into corners for tighter radii

generalJobShop.wireSelection: 0.1 to 0.3mm wire covers wide range of scope
generalJobShop.standardApproach: Zinc coated wire at medium price point for best cost/performance balance
generalJobShop.productivity: Focus on maximizing machine throughput if only one wire EDM in shop

taperCutting.prerequisite: MV1200R has tubular drive on U,V for best taper precision
taperCutting.maxAngleCheck: Control has built-in max angle verification feature

wireConsumption.annualImpact: Significant — wire consumption is the #1 operating expense

machineROI.driveWarranty: No ball screw replacement needed — ever
machineROI.maintenanceCost: Lower due to fewer wear items (no ball screws, no lubrication for drives)
